purpose: Reproducible preliminary bank-wide uniqueness and structural screening of the current non-destructive staging export and all replacement proposals.
interpretation: No normalized exact duplicate question stems were found within the 1,510 provisionally retained rows.
All 1,510 retained rows had a question, four non-empty options and an A-D answer key.
All 49 replacement proposals had a target ID, subject, question, exactly four options, an A-D answer key and an explanation.
No same-subject replacement-to-retained or replacement-to-replacement pair reached the preliminary word-trigram Dice threshold of 0.45.

This automated screen is not proof of academic correctness or complete semantic uniqueness. The 49 proposals still require contextual subject review; prior proposals already marked blocked or needing review remain in those statuses.
The bank is not deployment-ready: retained subject counts are below the 200-per-subject target and are uneven.
limitations: The 1,018 cross-window candidates below the earlier 0.65 manual-review threshold remain unreviewed.
The original within-window report retains a 279-candidate pending count and a 38-pair discrepancy against the reconstructed 390-candidate review set.
A zero-result automated similarity screen does not replace human review of wording, concepts, syllabus alignment, answer correctness or question quality.
